label: White House
sub: Center of Trump executive power. Site of hundreds of executive orders, press briefings, and key policy meetings across both terms.

label: US Capitol
sub: Site of Trump's two impeachments, both inaugurations, and the January 6, 2021 Capitol attack by supporters seeking to halt election certification.

label: US Supreme Court
sub: Trump appointed three justices (Gorsuch, Kavanaugh, Barrett), creating a 6-3 conservative majority. Key rulings include upholding Travel Ban, reversing Roe v. Wade, and granting presidential immunity.

label: Mar-a-Lago, Palm Beach FL
sub: Trump's private club and primary residence, used as the 'Winter White House' during both terms. Site of the August 2022 FBI search for classified documents and frequent foreign leader meetings.

label: Trump Tower, New York City
sub: Trump campaign headquarters in 2016 and symbolic HQ of the Trump Organization. Site of the 2016 Trump Tower meeting with Russians. Subject to NY AG and Manhattan DA investigations.

label: Manhattan Criminal Courthouse, NYC
sub: Site of Trump's 34-count felony hush money trial (2024). Trump became the first former US president convicted of felony crimes here on May 30, 2024.

label: Fulton County Courthouse, Atlanta GA
sub: Site of the Georgia RICO indictment (August 2023) of Trump and 18 co-defendants for alleged conspiracy to overturn Georgia's 2020 election results, including the recorded Raffensperger call.

label: Federal Courthouse, Miami FL
sub: Site of Trump's federal classified documents trial before Judge Aileen Cannon. The case (37 federal counts) was ultimately dismissed by Cannon in July 2024 citing concerns about the Special Counsel's appointment.

label: US District Court, Washington DC
sub: Site of Trump's federal January 6 indictment (4 counts including conspiracy). Special Counsel Jack Smith dropped the case in November 2024 per DOJ policy against indicting a sitting president-elect.

label: The Ellipse, Washington DC
sub: Site of the 'Save America' rally on January 6, 2021, where Trump gave a 70-minute speech urging supporters to march to the Capitol and 'fight like hell.' A key location in the incitement of insurrection case.

label: Pentagon, Arlington VA
sub: HQ of the Department of Defense. Multiple defense secretaries resigned or were fired under Trump. Site of controversies over military use at the US-Mexico border and Lafayette Square.

label: Eagle Pass, TX — Border Crossing
sub: One of the busiest and most contested US-Mexico border crossing points during Trump's immigration crackdowns. Texas Governor Abbott sent National Guard and placed buoys in the Rio Grande here; federal-state border confrontations became a major story.

label: El Paso, TX
sub: Major border city and key immigration processing hub. Site of the August 3, 2019 mass shooting at a Walmart targeting Hispanics, and overcrowded border processing facilities during surge years.

label: Laredo, TX — Border Port of Entry
sub: One of the largest US-Mexico land ports, processing billions in trade. Center of Trump administration's border enforcement efforts and subject to trade disruption from tariffs on Mexican imports.

label: Nogales, AZ — Border Crossing
sub: Key US-Mexico border port in Arizona. Site of significant border wall construction during Trump's first term and repeated large-scale migrant encounters. Connected to Trump's 'zero tolerance' family separation implementation.

label: McAllen, TX — Rio Grande Valley
sub: Rio Grande Valley border sector, consistently the highest-traffic corridor for illegal crossings during 2018-2023 surges. Site where family separation controversy was most acute in 2018.

label: Yuma, AZ — Border Sector
sub: Arizona border sector that saw dramatic migrant surge in 2021-2022. Trump focused on completing border wall sections in this area during his first term. Site of multiple 'field trip' visits by politicians.

label: San Diego — Tijuana Border
sub: Major urban border crossing and processing center. Site of 2018 migrant caravan confrontations and tear gas use on asylum seekers. One of the most fenced and monitored sections of the US-Mexico border.

label: Pittsburgh, PA — Steel Industry Hub
sub: Symbolic center of the US steel industry that Trump sought to protect with 25% steel tariffs (2018, 2025). Pennsylvania steel workers were key Trump political constituents; tariffs temporarily boosted domestic steel production.

label: Detroit, MI — Auto Industry
sub: Center of US auto manufacturing, heavily impacted by Trump tariff policies on steel, aluminum, and auto parts. Trump repeatedly targeted USMCA and auto trade with Canada and Mexico; the 2025 auto tariff threats destabilized supply chains.

label: Ames, IA — Farm Belt / Iowa Caucuses
sub: Iowa, a key Trump political base and major agricultural state, was severely impacted by China retaliatory tariffs on soybeans and corn. The administration created $28 billion in farm aid payments over 2018-2019 to offset trade war losses. Iowa also hosted the first Republican primary caucuses.

label: Port of Los Angeles, CA
sub: The largest US seaport by container volume, handling the majority of US-China trade. Trade disruptions from escalating tariffs caused significant shipping volume declines and supply chain disruptions throughout Trump's tariff campaigns.

label: Port of Seattle / Boeing HQ Area
sub: Home of Boeing, a major US exporter targeted by Chinese and EU retaliatory tariffs. Aerospace exports are among the most impacted by trade wars; the EU-US Airbus-Boeing dispute intensified under Trump.

label: Butler, PA — Assassination Attempt Site
sub: Site of the July 13, 2024 assassination attempt on Trump during a campaign rally. A gunman struck Trump's right ear, killed one attendee, and critically wounded two others before being shot by Secret Service. The iconic fist-raise photograph became an emblem of the 2024 campaign.

label: West Palm Beach, FL — Trump Golf Course
sub: Site of the September 15, 2024 second assassination attempt, where a Secret Service agent spotted a rifle-armed man in the bushes near Trump's golf course. The suspect was apprehended; Trump was not harmed.

label: Charlottesville, VA — Unite the Right Rally
sub: Site of the August 12, 2017 white supremacist rally that killed counter-protester Heather Heyer. Trump's 'very fine people on both sides' comment became one of the most controversial statements of his first term.

label: Lafayette Square, Washington DC
sub: On June 1, 2020, law enforcement using tear gas and batons cleared peaceful BLM protesters from Lafayette Square so Trump could walk to St. John's Church for a Bible photo op. The incident caused senior military and security officials to publicly distance themselves from Trump.

label: Minneapolis, MN — George Floyd Square
sub: Site of George Floyd's murder by police on May 25, 2020, sparking nationwide BLM protests. The incident prompted national debate over police reform and Trump's response — threatening to invoke the Insurrection Act — drew bipartisan criticism.

label: Kenosha, WI — BLM Protests / Kyle Rittenhouse
sub: Site of major BLM protests following the police shooting of Jacob Blake (August 23, 2020). Trump made multiple statements praising Kyle Rittenhouse, who shot three protesters. Trump visited Kenosha; Democrats said the visit inflamed tensions.

label: Walter Reed Medical Center, Bethesda MD
sub: Trump was hospitalized here for three days after contracting COVID-19 in October 2020. He received experimental monoclonal antibody treatment and steroids. His dramatic balcony return — removing his mask — generated widespread controversy.

label: Trump National Golf Club, Bedminster NJ
sub: Trump's New Jersey golf property, frequently used as a 'Summer White House.' Site of major fundraisers, foreign leader meetings, and LIV Golf events. Trump spent significant time here during both terms.

label: Iowa — 2024 Primary Caucus
sub: Trump won the January 2024 Iowa Republican caucuses with 51% of the vote — the highest share in Iowa caucus history — effectively ending the primary contest. Iowa was also a key swing state Trump won in 2016 and 2020.

label: New Hampshire — 2024 Republican Primary
sub: Trump won the New Hampshire Republican primary in January 2024 against Nikki Haley, his last remaining major primary challenger. Despite Haley's relative success (41%), Trump's dominance effectively secured the nomination.

label: Milwaukee, WI — 2024 Republican National Convention
sub: The 2024 Republican National Convention was held in Milwaukee July 15-18. Trump appeared with his ear bandaged from the assassination attempt, accepted the nomination, and selected JD Vance as running mate. The convention cemented the MAGA movement's complete dominance of the Republican Party.

label: Dover Air Force Base, DE
sub: Site of dignified transfer ceremonies for US military fallen. Trump attended multiple ceremonies here. The contrast between his respectful presence and his reported 2020 comments calling fallen soldiers 'suckers and losers' (denied by Trump) became a major controversy.

label: Harley-Davidson HQ, Milwaukee WI
sub: Harley-Davidson was among the first US companies to announce production moves abroad (to Thailand) in response to EU retaliatory tariffs on motorcycles (in response to Trump's steel tariffs). Trump threatened to tax Harley-Davidson 'like never before' for moving jobs out.

label: Boeing Plant, North Charleston SC
sub: Major US aerospace manufacturing site. Boeing's 787 Dreamliner production here benefited from Trump's 'Buy American' rhetoric but faced headwinds from tariff-driven supply chain disruptions and China's retaliatory tariffs on US aircraft.

label: Foxconn Site, Mount Pleasant WI
sub: Trump personally promoted Foxconn's promised $10 billion factory that would create 13,000 jobs in Wisconsin. The deal received massive state tax subsidies but Foxconn scaled back dramatically and ultimately built a far smaller facility, becoming a symbol of unmet manufacturing promises.

label: El Salvador CECOT Prison (via US Deal)
sub: Trump struck a deal with El Salvador's President Bukele to house Venezuelan deportees at CECOT, the mega-prison complex. Hundreds of Venezuelans deported under the Alien Enemies Act were sent here in March 2025, triggering legal battles over due process and human rights.

label: Arizona/Sonora Border — Wall Construction
sub: Central location for border wall construction activity during Trump's first term. Over 450 miles of new or replacement barrier was built, primarily in Arizona, California, and New Mexico. Trump declared the wall built; critics noted much was replacement, not new.

label: US Treasury Department, Washington DC
sub: Headquarters for tariff and sanctions policy under both Trump terms. Treasury Secretaries Steve Mnuchin (1st term) and Scott Bessent (2nd term) managed trade negotiations with China, Canada, Mexico, and others amid tariff escalations. In March 2026, Treasury issued General License U lifting sanctions on 140M barrels of Iranian oil to tame energy prices.

label: DHS Headquarters, Washington DC
sub: Headquarters of the Department of Homeland Security. Center of a major funding crisis beginning mid-February 2026: DHS funding lapsed, sending 480+ TSA officers to quit, creating 40%+ absences at some airports and hour-long security lines. Congress failed to pass clean funding for weeks. Trump signed an EO to restore TSA pay in March 2026.

label: Palm Beach Intl Airport — Renamed for Trump
sub: Florida Gov. DeSantis signed legislation on March 31, 2026 renaming Palm Beach International Airport as 'President Donald J. Trump International Airport,' pending FAA approval by July 1. The airport serves the greater Palm Beach area near Mar-a-Lago, Trump's primary residence.

label: National Mall, DC — 'No Kings' Protests (Mar 28, 2026)
sub: Site of the Washington D.C. anchor event of the March 28, 2026 'No Kings' mass protests. More than 3,100 protest events took place simultaneously across all 50 states, with organizers reporting millions of participants — among the largest demonstrations of Trump's second term. Protesters cited the Iran war, tariff-driven cost of living increases, DHS shutdown chaos, and Trump's use of executive power.

label: Washington Hilton, DC — WHCD Shooting (Apr 25, 2026)
sub: On April 25, 2026, gunman Cole Tomas Allen, 31, breached security at the Washington Hilton during the White House Correspondents' Dinner and fired shots. Trump, Vance, and cabinet members were evacuated; one Secret Service officer was struck (protected by vest). Allen — carrying a shotgun, handgun, and knives — was subdued. Acting AG Blanche said Allen was likely targeting Trump administration officials. The shooting prompted Trump to call for a secure White House ballroom.

label: 2nd Circuit Court, Foley Square NYC
sub: On April 28, 2026, the Second Circuit unanimously rejected the Trump administration's mandatory ICE detention policy — ruling immigrants caught entering without inspection cannot be detained indefinitely without bond hearings. The ruling creates a circuit split with the 11th Circuit, setting up a likely Supreme Court showdown. The court also heard challenges to deportation procedures in 2025-2026.

label: Phoenix, AZ — Border Security Expo (May 7, 2026)
sub: Site of the Border Security Expo (May 7, 2026) where White House Border Czar Tom Homan pledged 'mass deportations are coming.' Homan highlighted ICE's ~1,200 arrests/day pace and plans to expand detention to 70,000 daily, ahead of the Senate's $72B ICE/CBP reconciliation vote the week of May 11.

label: Havana, Cuba — Sanctions EO (May 7, 2026)
sub: Trump signed an Executive Order on May 7, 2026 (Federal Register 2026-09173) imposing a new sanctions framework on Cuban regime officials for political repression and threats to US national security. The EO targeted Cuba's security apparatus, human rights violators, and foreign banks transacting with the Cuban government — citing Cuba's alignment with Iran, harboring of foreign intelligence operations near US territory, and destabilizing migration patterns.

label: Baton Rouge, LA — Senate Primary (May 16, 2026)
sub: Site of the May 16, 2026 Louisiana Republican Senate primary where Trump-backed Rep. Julia Letlow (~45%) defeated incumbent Sen. Bill Cassidy — one of seven GOP senators who voted to convict Trump in the 2021 impeachment trial. State Treasurer John Fleming (~28%) also advanced to a June 27 runoff with Letlow; Cassidy finished third (~25%). The result was the first Senate primary defeat of a sitting Republican senator in nearly a decade and a demonstration of MAGA's grip on the party primary electorate.

label: Northern Kentucky (KY-04) — Gallrein Defeats Massie (May 19-20, 2026)
sub: Trump-backed challenger Ed Gallrein (former Navy SEAL) defeated seven-term incumbent Rep. Thomas Massie on May 19-20, 2026 by approximately 9 points — the most expensive House primary in US history ($32.6M total). The decisive MAGA primary victory demonstrates Trump's ~82% endorsement win rate holds even against well-known deep-red incumbents. Massie had clashed with Trump over the Iran war, 'One Big Beautiful Bill,' and Epstein file release.

label: Havana, Cuba — Sanctions Designations (May 19, 2026)
sub: On May 19, 2026, the Trump administration designated 11 Cuban government officials and 3 security/intelligence agencies under the existing Cuba sanctions framework. Targets include the National Assembly president, ministers of communications and justice, the minister of interior, the deputy defense minister, three generals, the intelligence director, and the National Revolutionary Police chief. Secretary Rubio warned further designations are coming. Cuba condemned the actions as a 'fraudulent case' for potential military action.

label: US Treasury — Banking Immigration EO (May 20, 2026)
sub: On May 20, 2026, Trump signed 'Restoring Integrity to America's Financial System' directing Treasury and federal regulators to require banks to factor customers' immigration status in financial risk assessments. The EO specifically flags ITIN use (associated with undocumented workers) as a risk indicator. Treasury has 90 days to propose updated Bank Secrecy Act regulations. Civil liberties groups argue the order will functionally exclude undocumented immigrants from the banking system.

label: State Department, DC — Taiwan Arms Sale & Iran Deal Diplomacy (May 22, 2026)
sub: On May 22, 2026, the State Department is managing two simultaneous high-stakes diplomatic tracks: (1) Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te publicly confirmed he would be 'happy' to speak with Trump ahead of a decision on a $14B arms sale — a potentially historic first US-Taiwan presidential call since 1979; (2) Al-Arabiya reported a leaked 'final draft' of a US-Iran peace agreement via Pakistan mediation, claiming a deal announcement was 'imminent within hours.' Secretary Rubio overseeing both tracks.

label: USCIS HQ, Camp Springs MD — Green Card AOS Policy Memo (May 23, 2026)
sub: On May 23, 2026, USCIS issued a sweeping policy memo eliminating routine 'adjustment of status' (AOS) as a green card pathway — requiring approximately 500,000 legal visa holders per year (H-1B workers, F-1 students, humanitarian parolees) to leave the US and apply through a US consulate abroad. The memo treats AOS as an 'extraordinary form of administrative grace' available only in exceptional circumstances — a major expansion of immigration restrictions beyond undocumented immigrants to include legal visa holders. Legal challenges citing APA violations and statutory misreading of the INA are expected.

label: Arlington National Cemetery — Memorial Day 2026
sub: On May 26, 2026 (Memorial Day), Trump presided over the annual wreath-laying ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery and the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier — the first Memorial Day since the US-Iran war began February 28, 2026. Defense Secretary Hegseth, VP Vance, and Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine attended. The ceremony honored the seven US service members killed in the Iran conflict. Trump posted on Truth Social targeting 'Dumocrats who disrespect our Military.'

label: CIA Headquarters, Langley VA — Rush Arrest (May 28, 2026)
sub: The FBI on May 28, 2026 arrested senior CIA official David Rush after discovering 400+ gold bars worth $40M+, dozens of luxury watches, and $2M cash at his Virginia home. Rush faces charges of criminal theft of government money — raising profound questions about CIA internal oversight. The case represents one of the largest alleged thefts by a US intelligence official in recent history.

label: SDNY Federal Courthouse — DOJ Carroll Perjury Probe (May 28, 2026)
sub: The DOJ under Acting AG Todd Blanche opened a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll on May 28, 2026, focusing on alleged perjury in her civil suit testimony against Trump — the same courthouse district where Carroll's civil cases were litigated. Carroll won approximately $88M in damages across two civil trials; Trump is appealing both verdicts. Critics call the probe politically motivated retaliation by DOJ against a Trump accuser who prevailed in court.

label: Fox News HQ, New York City — Trump 'Shouldn't Have Been in Iran' Interview (Jun 1, 2026)
sub: Site of the June 1, 2026 Fox News interview (with Lara Trump) in which President Trump made a stunning reversal, saying 'We shouldn't have been there in the first place... We shouldn't have been in Iran' — directly contradicting his justification for launching Operation Epic Fury on Feb. 28, 2026. Trump also claimed the US 'left Iran's military alone' and described Iran's military as 'somewhat moderate.' The interview aired as Iran's IRGC threatened to suspend indirect talks with the US.

label: ODNI Liberty Crossing, McLean VA — Pulte Acting DNI
sub: Headquarters of the Office of the Director of National Intelligence. On June 2, 2026, Trump named FHFA director Bill Pulte as acting DNI, replacing Tulsi Gabbard who announced her resignation effective June 30. Pulte has no intelligence background; Senate Minority Leader Schumer called him 'a partisan thug with no experience in intelligence.'

label: NBC Studios, 30 Rock NYC — Trump 'Meet the Press' (Jun 7, 2026)
sub: On June 7, 2026 (Day 504 / Iran War Day 99), Trump appeared on NBC 'Meet the Press' with Kristen Welker, laying out his clearest Iran deal framework yet: no early sanctions relief or asset unfreeze; will help Iran destroy its ~440.9 kg of 60%-enriched uranium stockpile if a deal is reached. Iran's supreme leader adviser told CNN talks were 'at a deadlock.' The interview aired as the US shot down 6 Iranian drones and struck radar sites on Goruk and Qeshm Islands over the prior 48 hours.

label: US Supreme Court — 3-1 Rulings vs. Trump, Agency Power Win (Jun 29, 2026)
sub: Supreme Court overturned Humphrey's Executor 6-3, cementing Trump's power to fire independent agency officials without cause; declined to hear his E. Jean Carroll appeal ($5M verdict stands); upheld Mississippi's mail-in ballot law 5-4. Fed Governor Lisa Cook separately allowed to remain.

label: The White House — 50% Canada Tariffs Announced, Effective Aug 19 (Jul 20, 2026)
sub: Trump announced 50% Section 338 tariffs on Canadian dairy, alcohol, furniture, and motor vehicles, effective Aug 19, 2026 — roughly $16-20B in annual imports affected. Same day, EO 14415 delegated Defense Production Act authority over critical minerals.

label: USTR — Section 301 Forced-Labor Tariffs on 80+ Countries Take Effect (Jul 23, 2026)
sub: USTR finalized Section 301 forced-labor tariffs (10-12.5%) on more than 80 trading partners including Canada, Mexico, India, and the UK, replacing the expired temporary 10% Section 122 global tariff.

label: Columbia, TN — Rep. Andy Ogles Loses GOP Primary Despite Trump Endorsement (Aug 6, 2026)
sub: Trump-endorsed Rep. Andy Ogles (TN-5), under federal campaign-finance investigation, lost his Republican primary to establishment-backed Charlie Hatcher, 47%-53% — the third sitting House Republican defeated in a 2026 primary.

label: US Capitol — Senate Passes 90-6 Stopgap Funding Bill, SAVE Act Punted (Aug 8, 2026)
sub: Senate voted 90-6 to extend federal funding through Dec 11, averting a pre-midterm shutdown fight. Trump's SAVE America Act (proof-of-citizenship voting bill) was deferred to September after Trump had demanded the Senate cancel its recess to pass it.

label: Kennedy Center — Board Votes to Restore Trump's Name, Close for 2-Year Renovation (Aug 13, 2026)
sub: Trump-appointed board voted to add 'Restored and Renovated by President Donald J. Trump' inscription and close the building until 2028 for a $250M renovation, months after a judge ordered Trump's name removed.

label: Washington, D.C. — Judge Sullivan Warns DOJ of Contempt Over Epstein Files (Aug 13, 2026)
sub: US District Judge Emmet Sullivan pressed DOJ attorneys on compliance with orders to publish redaction justifications and turn over withheld materials under the Epstein Files Transparency Act.

label: The Pentagon — Trump Orders Navy to Revert to Steam Catapults on Newest Carriers (Aug 14, 2026)
sub: National security memorandum directs removal of EMALS from Ford-class carriers starting with USS Doris Miller, reverting to steam catapults despite Navy/industry opposition over billions in added cost.

label: The White House — 50% Canada Tariffs Paused 3 Days as Deal Finalized (Aug 19, 2026)
sub: Trump announced a three-day pause on the 50% Section 338 tariffs on Canadian goods that had been set to take effect Aug 19, saying the US and Canada had reached a trade deal 'subject to the finalization of documents.'

label: Washington, D.C. — Judge Blocks Trump's Teen Pregnancy Prevention Overhaul (Aug 19, 2026)
sub: US District Judge Christopher Cooper granted a preliminary injunction blocking HHS's abstinence-only overhaul of the Teen Pregnancy Prevention Program, after the agency canceled 53 of 67 grants in June.

label: Federal Reserve, Washington D.C. — Senate Democrats Press Warsh to Disclose Trump Calls (Aug 19, 2026)
sub: Four Democratic senators demanded Fed Chair Kevin Warsh disclose any conversations with Trump since taking the role in May 2026, after reports of undisclosed calls despite his calendar showing none.

label: The White House — Trump Declares 'Most Crushing' Economic Operation Against Iran (Aug 20, 2026)
sub: Trump said the US would launch 'the MOST CRUSHING ECONOMIC OPERATION EVER TAKEN AGAINST ANY COUNTRY' against Iran, threatening 'TREMENDOUS Economic Consequences' for any nation providing Tehran a financial lifeline.

label: US Treasury Department — National Debt Surpasses $40 Trillion (Aug 19, 2026)
sub: Treasury's daily statement showed total public debt outstanding crossing $40.05 trillion, months earlier than forecasters expected, partly due to lost tariff revenue after SCOTUS struck down the IEEPA tariffs.

label: The White House — US-Canada Trade Talks Collapse, 50% Tariffs Take Effect (Aug 21, 2026)
sub: Talks between Washington and Ottawa fell apart late Friday night; 50% Section 338 tariffs on roughly $20 billion of Canadian goods took effect, reversing the Aug 18 'deal' announcement.

label: Myrtle Beach, SC — Trump Rallies for Darline Graham Ahead of Senate Runoff (Aug 21, 2026)
sub: Trump held an 80-minute rally at the Myrtle Beach Convention Center campaigning for Sen. Darline Graham ahead of her Aug 25 GOP runoff against Rep. Ralph Norman.

label: Washington, D.C. — Court Strikes Down Trump Visa Ban Affecting South Asian Nations (Aug 22, 2026)
sub: A US federal court struck down Trump's visa ban targeting several South Asian nations, ruling it exceeded executive authority.

label: Washington, D.C. — Trump Administration Seeks to Block BBC Subpoena of Ivanka Trump and Donald Trump Jr. (Aug 22, 2026)
sub: The administration moved to block a BBC subpoena targeting Ivanka Trump and Donald Trump Jr., broadening its legal battles with media organizations.

label: The White House — Trump Raises Canada Auto, Parts & Steel Tariffs to 50% Starting Jan 1, 2027 (Aug 24, 2026)
sub: Trump said tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks, auto parts, and steel would rise to 50% on Jan 1, 2027, doubling the current 25% rate, after trade talks collapsed.

label: US Treasury Department — Bessent Unveils 'Economic D-Day' Iran Sanctions (Aug 24, 2026)
sub: Treasury Secretary Bessent unveiled sweeping new sanctions targeting Iran and countries still trading with Tehran; Iran threatened to seize ships in the Strait of Hormuz in response.

label: The White House — Trump Signs Order Renaming Lake Ontario 'Lake America' (Aug 27, 2026)
sub: Trump signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario 'Lake America,' escalating the trade fight with Canada; PM Mark Carney rejected the move.

label: Houston, TX — Trump Headlines RNC Fundraiser for Ken Paxton's Senate Bid (Aug 27, 2026)
sub: Trump headlined a closed-press RNC fundraiser in Houston boosting Texas AG Ken Paxton's Senate campaign, tickets up to nearly $500,000.
